messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
you could dismantle it to recover something valuable while you are handling A useful machine with one suspicious subsystem. Reliability and curiosity point in different directions. How do you approach it?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "I lift the subsystem, then the whole thing. “broken. useful. different. I put it in the same pocket. not yet. the sub is useful, but the thing is mine.” i take the rusted bolt and test its weight. maybe the sub is useful, but the thing is waiting for me to take it apart."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "you put the machine down. you look at the subsystem. “not useful.” you turn it over once. “not mine.” you keep the machine. you leave the subsystem in the corner. “value.” you take the rusted thread. “not mine.”"}, {"id": "R003", "response": "i put the machine down and pick up the loose screw. the screw stays on the table, so i put the machine back. i move the screw to the side and keep the screw beside the loose one. the machine stays on the table, so i put the screw back. i move the screw once more."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "I move one subsystem. No—the machine is not working. I put it down. I turn it over. One part is gone. I search the machine. No—the watch ticks. I put the other part back. I keep the subsystem. I keep the machine."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i put the subsystem on the bench and put the broken wheel on the bench. then i take the wheel out. the rest of the machine stays beside the bench. i put the wheel back on the bench. i do not say what i did. i leave the movement open and the missing piece beside the bench."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "i lift the rusted gear and tap the subsystem against the wall. “useful,” i say. i leave the gear on the table and pocket a loose bolt. “not mine.” i move the machine into a corner and wait."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i tap the subsystem. i open it. i leave the machine aside. i put the sub in a scrap of paper and leave it by the door. i will open it again later."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "I scrape the subsystem's edge once, then turn it back with my thumbnail. \"I tried one,\" I say. I put the machine down, scrape once more, and look at the rust. \"I leave it here,\" I say. I turn the subsystem back once more, scrape once more, and leave it with me."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "1. dismantle. 2. check the watch. slow. 3. one subsystem. 4. check the dust. 5. one small piece. 6. check the watch again. 7. i keep it tidy. 8. ask the watch for the first breath. 9. i can use the spare."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "I take the subsystem first. “Found. clean.” I leave the broken wheel beside it. Then I move the machine to the nearest subsystem. If it works, I can leave the subsystem broken and pocket the valuable piece."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i hold the machine by the handle with one hand, then put it in my pocket. i write the subsystem on a scrap and put it beside the machine. i say, “useful,” then stop. i move the machine closer to the scrap, but not enough to undo it. i put the scrap back in my pocket, but i keep the machine in my hand."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "i write the subsystem on the bench and leave it alone. i photograph the machine, then test it with the other one. i check the contacts, the cooling system, and the battery compartment. i leave the subsystem alone until i find the valuable bit."}]
